description: Four-step sequencer whose step moves on at random rather than on a trigger, with a level knob and an output for each step and a further output carrying a note voltage

params.text: Sets the voltage this step sends to its own output, 0 to 10V
Sets how far the note output is moved at random, from no movement at 0 to twelve semitones either way at full

inputs.text: A fresh random number from 0 to 1 is compared with this voltage every sample and the step moves on when the number is larger, so 0V runs the sequence and 1V stops it; no trigger edge is read
A rising edge sets the sequence back to the first step; it reads high above 1V

outputs.text: Carries the voltage set by the knob for that step while the sequence stands on it, and 0V at every other step
Carries the step's place in a fixed pattern turned into a note number, converted to a frequency in hertz and divided by twelve; it lands between about 0.3V and 1.5V and is not a volt per octave

notes: the sequence runs by itself: with nothing patched into Trigger the step changes in nearly every sample, so the four step outputs carry a burst rather than a sequence
the note output is worked out afresh in every sample, so with the randomness knob above 0 it carries a new random value at the sample rate rather than one value per step
Reset is the only jack that reads an edge

inputs.0:
0 to 1V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
